Introduction to AEKO Chain.title: Introduction to AEKO Chain
Introduction to AEKO Chain.html:
Introduction to AEKO Chain

Status: the canonical public deployment documented by this repository is the AEKO Public Testnet.

AEKO Chain is an SVM-compatible Layer-1 codebase with native runtime programs for tokens, permissions and SocialFi, plus SBF program loaders for externally deployed Rust on-chain programs.

Execution

The runtime supports Sealevel-style parallel execution and SBF program loading. This documentation does not assert an unverified fixed TPS or finality number.

Permission primitives

Permission, revocation, wallet-permission and related native programs are registered in the runtime. Operational identity issuance still depends on the surrounding application and issuer workflow.

Architecture Overview.title: Architecture Overview
Architecture Overview.html:
Architecture Overview

AEKO's architecture consists of three primary layers working in unison:

1. The Execution Layer (SVM)

A forked and optimized version of the AEKO Virtual Machine. It handles transaction processing, smart contract execution, and state management. It utilizes Proof of History (PoH) for timekeeping and Sealevel for parallel transaction processing.

2. The Permission Layer

A set of native eBPF programs that intercept transactions before they reach the execution state. It validates user Clearance Levels (L0-L5) and enforces compliance rules defined by the network or specific dApps.

3. The Social Graph Layer

An indexed data layer that maps on-chain identities to social interactions. It uses Content Signatures to verify the authenticity of posts and interactions, feeding into the Reputation Protocol.

Wallet Setup.title: Wallet Setup
Wallet Setup.html:
Wallet Setup

Use an AEKO-compatible Ed25519 keypair for the public testnet. The repository-supported path is the AEKO CLI/keygen toolchain; third-party wallet support must be verified independently before it is advertised.

CLI wallet

# Install the release CLI bundle on Linux
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MilliHub-dev/aeko-chain/main/install/aeko-cli-install.sh | sh

# Generate a keypair
aeko-keygen new --outfile ~/.config/aeko/id.json

# Select the deployed public testnet
aeko config set --url testnet

The testnet moniker resolves to https://rpc.aeko.online in the current CLI code.

Testnet Funding.title: Testnet Funding
Testnet Funding.html:
Testnet Funding

Public test AEKO is issued through the policy-controlled Funding Portal. The private Faucet Daemon is an internal TCP signer and has no public URL.

Public Funding Portal

https://fund.aeko.online enforces wallet cooldown and daily-budget policy. Explorer Network Tools live separately at /network-tools.

Open Testnet Funding Portal

HTTP request

curl -X POST https://fund.aeko.online/api/funding/request \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"address":"<recipient-address>"}'

On the deployed public testnet, low-level requestAirdrop is reserved for the server-side Funding Gateway. Local/custom test validators may leave that authorization disabled for developer testing.

Identity & Clearance.title: Identity & Clearance Levels
Identity & Clearance.html:
Identity & Clearance

Implemented primitive: the permission-types crate defines a six-tier ClearanceTier and a non-transferable ClearanceSbt account model. Permission-registry verifies issuer/tier/expiry state.
TierCode labelMeaning in current source
L0PublicImplicit; no SBT stored.
L1VerifiedHumanVerified-human credential tier.
L2KycKYC/financial credential tier.
L3EnterpriseEnterprise credential tier.
L4GovernmentGovernment credential tier.
L5MilitaryHighest clearance tier in the current enum.

These code labels are protocol data types. A production issuer/KYC/biometric workflow is a separate operational system and should not be inferred from the enum alone.

Gatekeeper Programs.title: Gatekeeper Programs
Gatekeeper Programs.html:
Permission Programs

AEKO registers permission-related native programs including wallet-permissions, permission-registry, revocation-registry and subnet-registry. Use their concrete program IDs and instruction/state contracts rather than a generic "gatekeeper" service assumption.

The term gatekeeper is descriptive documentation language; it is not the name of a standalone deployed program in the current runtime list.

Soulbound Tokens.title: Soulbound Tokens
Soulbound Tokens.html:
Clearance SBT Accounts

The current permission-types code defines ClearanceSbt, a non-transferable account bound to a holder, tier, issuer, issue slot, optional expiry and revocation registry. Permission-registry contains verification logic for active, non-expired SBTs.

This is an implemented on-chain data/verification primitive. It does not by itself prove that a public identity issuer, KYC provider or biometric enrollment service is deployed.

Compliance Hooks.title: Compliance Hooks
Compliance Hooks.html:
Permission Enforcement

Current enforcement is implemented through concrete permission/revocation/subnet program logic and runtime checks. Do not treat "compliance hooks" as a generic plugin API unless a specific program or runtime integration documents that behavior.

Regulatory compliance is an application/legal outcome, not something this repository can guarantee merely because permission primitives exist.

Content Layer Storage.title: Content Layer Storage
Content Layer Storage.html:
Content Layer Storage

AEKO utilizes a hybrid storage model to handle the massive data requirements of SocialFi applications efficiently.

On-Chain (Hot)

Critical metadata, content hashes, and interaction pointers are stored directly in AEKO account state for sub-second access.

Off-Chain (Cold)

Actual media files (images, videos) and long-form text are stored on decentralized networks like Arweave or IPFS, anchored by their hashes on AEKO.

Reputation Protocol.title: Reputation Protocol
Reputation Protocol.html:
Reputation Design

Status: design-level concept. The runtime registers SocialFi posts, rewards, staking, anti-spam and monetization programs, but there is no standalone reputation native program in the current runtime built-in list.

Applications may derive reputation from on-chain activity, but any score, weighting formula or governance effect must be treated as application policy unless backed by a specific deployed program/state contract.

Proof of Engagement.title: Proof of Engagement
Proof of Engagement.html:
Engagement Data & Rewards

AEKO SocialFi code contains posts/engagement state plus separate rewards, staking, anti-spam and monetization programs. "Proof of Engagement" is a product/design label, not a separate consensus mechanism in the current validator runtime.

When documenting rewards, reference the concrete SocialFi program instruction/state that enforces the behavior.

Content Signatures.title: Content Signatures
Content Signatures.html:
Content Signatures

Status: not a standalone deployed runtime feature in the current program list.

Transactions and wallet actions are cryptographically signed as usual. A separate end-to-end content-attestation protocol should be documented as planned/design work unless a concrete program, account schema and verification path are present and deployed.

AEKO SVM Runtime.title: AEKO SVM Runtime
AEKO SVM Runtime.html:
AEKO SVM Runtime

The core of AEKO Chain is a highly optimized fork of the Aeko Virtual Machine (SVM). It is designed to handle the high throughput required for social media scale.

Key Optimizations

  • Compute Budget: Increased compute units per block to allow for complex social graph traversals.
  • Account Indexing: Native indexing for social relationships (followers/following).
  • Fee Markets: Localized fee markets prevent one viral dApp from congesting the entire network.

Sealevel Parallelization.title: Sealevel Parallelization
Sealevel Parallelization.html:
Sealevel Parallelization

Unlike EVM chains that process transactions sequentially, AEKO uses Sealevel to process thousands of smart contracts in parallel.

Transactions describe all the states they will read or write during execution. This allows the runtime to find non-overlapping transactions and execute them concurrently, utilizing all available validator cores.

Consensus Mechanism.title: Consensus Mechanism
Consensus Mechanism.html:
Consensus Mechanism

AEKO uses Proof of History (PoH) combined with Tower BFT to achieve consensus.

Proof of History

A cryptographic clock that allows validators to agree on the passage of time without communicating. This reduces messaging overhead and enables sub-second block times.

Tower BFT

A PBFT-like consensus algorithm that leverages the PoH clock to reach finality quickly. Validators vote on forks, and votes have a lock-out period that increases exponentially.

Validator Guide.title: Validator Guide
Validator Guide.html:
Validator Guide

Help secure the AEKO network by running a validator node. Validators earn rewards for processing transactions and participating in consensus.

Requirements

  • CPU: 12+ cores / 24+ threads (AMD Ryzen 9 or Threadripper recommended).
  • RAM: 128GB+ DDR4/DDR5.
  • Storage: 2TB+ NVMe SSD (PCIe Gen4).
  • Clearance: L3 (Citizen) Identity Verification.

Rust SDK.title: Rust SDK
Rust SDK.html:
Rust SDK

The primary language for developing on AEKO is Rust. The AEKO SDK provides all the necessary tools to write, test, and deploy high-performance programs.

Example Program

use aeko_program::{
    account_info::AccountInfo,
    entrypoint,
    entrypoint::ProgramResult,
    pubkey::Pubkey,
};

entrypoint!(process_instruction);

fn process_instruction(
    program_id: &Pubkey,
    accounts: &[AccountInfo],
    instruction_data: &[u8],
) -> ProgramResult {
    // Your logic here
    Ok(())
}

Program Architecture.title: Program Architecture
Program Architecture.html:
Program Architecture

AEKO programs are stateless. All state is stored in separate 'Accounts' passed to the program during execution.

Key Components

  • Program ID: The public key of the executable account.
  • Instruction Data: A byte array containing the command and arguments.
  • Accounts: The data accounts the program will read from or write to.

Native Syscalls.title: Native Syscalls
Native Syscalls.html:
Native Runtime Helpers

AEKO's permission-layer design calls for native runtime helpers that expose clearance levels and verify content signatures without routing through general-purpose programs.

  • Clearance-level lookup for transaction gating.
  • Content-signature verification for social proofs and moderation workflows.

Security Best Practices.title: Security Best Practices
Security Best Practices.html:
Security Best Practices

Writing secure smart contracts is critical. Follow these guidelines to prevent exploits.

  • Check Signers: Always verify that critical accounts have signed the transaction.
  • Validate Owners: Ensure accounts are owned by the expected program.
  • Integer Overflow: Use checked_add and checked_sub for math operations.
  • PDA Validation: Always derive Program Derived Addresses on-chain to verify they are correct.

Write Your First Program.title: Write Your First Program
Write Your First Program.html:
Write Your First Program

AEKO now includes a minimal external developer path for writing on-chain Rust programs. The starter template lives in contracts/hello-aeko-program and is paired with a walkthrough in docs/developer-sdk/write-your-first-program.md.

Starter Flow

  • Use aeko-program as the on-chain SDK surface.
  • Build the starter contract for the AEKO SBF target.
  • Deploy with aeko program deploy once your wallet and testnet RPC are configured.

What You Get

A minimal starter contract, a deploy path, and a first invoke example so outside teams can get from repo clone to first program faster.

Deploy And Invoke On Testnet.title: Deploy And Invoke On Testnet
Deploy And Invoke On Testnet.html:
Deploy And Invoke On Testnet

The developer docs now include a full deploy-and-invoke walkthrough for the starter AEKO program. It covers building the contract, deploying it to testnet, and invoking it with the provided Rust example.

aeko program deploy <program-binary> --url testnet
  • Use the starter invoke example in contracts/hello-aeko-program/examples/invoke_hello.rs.
  • Record the deployed program id and transaction signatures for your own operator notes.
  • Point your local CLI and SDKs at the same testnet RPC when validating the flow.

Audience

This path is for external developers who want a practical first smart contract experience on AEKO without reverse-engineering the monorepo.

Identity & DID.title: Identity & DID
Identity & DID.html:
Identity & DID

Phase 4 starts with identity as the foundation for wallets, permissions, and SDKs. AEKO uses the wallet address as the primary identity anchor and resolves decentralized identifiers in the form did:aeko:<wallet_pubkey>.

Identity Anchor

The wallet public key remains the root identity reference across wallet core, delegated permissions, SDKs, and testnet validation.

Optional KYC

Off-chain verification may be anchored on-chain as a hash, while keeping raw identity data out of public account state.

Phase 4 Source of Truth

The wallet and SDK stack now builds on the signed-off identity model in docs/wallet/identity.md.

Wallet Core.title: Wallet Core
Wallet Core.html:
Wallet Core

AEKO wallet core now includes mnemonic generation, encrypted keystore export/import, transaction and message signing, stateless signing, and Ledger-backed account support in the Rust wallet-core crate.

Current Capabilities

  • BIP39 mnemonic-backed wallet creation and restore
  • Encrypted keystore roundtrip with versioned metadata
  • Transaction signing, batch signing, and message signing
  • Stateless payload signing for higher-assurance environments
  • Ledger device discovery and hardware-backed signing path

Validation Path

The repo now includes a wallet-core validation helper example plus a testnet runbook so operators can record final evidence in the Phase 4 closeout record.

Wallet Permissions.title: Wallet Permissions
Wallet Permissions.html:
Wallet Permissions

AEKO wallet permissions are now implemented as a dedicated on-chain program with owner, spender, and viewer roles; spend caps; allowlists; time-bounded delegates; emergency freeze; and an audit log.

Policy Controls

  • Per-transaction and daily AEKO caps
  • Per-token spend caps
  • Program and token allowlists
  • Valid-from and valid-until epochs

Auditability

  • Grant, update, revoke, freeze, and unfreeze events
  • Usage recording windows
  • Deterministic effective-permission reads

Closeout Focus

The remaining blocker is end-to-end testnet validation of initialization, grant/update/revoke flows, effective reads, spend-limit enforcement, and freeze behavior.

Explorer API.title: Explorer API
Explorer API.html:
Explorer API

AEKO now has a first-pass explorer backend with HTTP routes for blocks, transactions, token summaries, collection summaries, account profiles, creator profiles, posts, NFTs, staking, engagement, and search.

  • GET /blocks and GET /blocks/{slot}
  • GET /transactions and GET /transactions/{signature}
  • GET /tokens/{mint} and GET /tokens/transfers
  • GET /collections/{collectionId} and GET /nfts/{tokenId}
  • GET /accounts/{address} and GET /creators/{address}
  • GET /posts/{postId} and GET /search

Frontend Binding

The web app can consume this backend when VITE_AEKO_TESTNET_EXPLORER_API or VITE_AEKO_MAINNET_EXPLORER_API is configured.

Local Boot Path

Run cargo run -p aeko-explorer-backend --example api_server and point the web app at http://127.0.0.1:8088 to exercise the current explorer stack locally.

Explorer Web.title: Explorer Web
Explorer Web.html:
Explorer Web

The web app now includes backend-aware explorer pages for dashboard, block detail, transaction detail, account profiles, creator profiles, post anchors, AEKO-721 token views, AEKO-721 collection views, and AEKO-20 token views.

  • /explorer dashboard with search, network switch, query-driven filters, and first-pass newer/older navigation for blocks, transactions, and posts
  • /explorer/block/:height and /explorer/tx/:hash
  • /explorer/account/:address and /explorer/creator/:address
  • /explorer/post/:postId, /explorer/nft/:tokenId, /explorer/collection/:collectionId, and /explorer/token/:mint

Current Model

These pages use the explorer backend when configured and otherwise fail honestly with configuration guidance instead of pretending live data exists.

SocialFi RPC.title: SocialFi RPC
SocialFi RPC.html:
SocialFi RPC

Phase 5 now includes SocialFi-specific RPC reads and write wrappers for creator rewards, claimable rewards, reputation, engagement, post anchors, and social staking.

  • Reads: creator rewards, claimable rewards, engagement score, engagement events, reputation score, post anchors, creator posts, social stake positions
  • Writes: submitEngagementProof, stakeBehindCreator, unstakeBehindCreator, claimSocialStakeYield

Implementation Boundary

The RPC layer maps directly onto the SocialFi support programs and validates signed transactions before forwarding write requests into the normal submission pipeline.

Aeko Social Backend Integration.title: Aeko Social Backend Integration
Aeko Social Backend Integration.html:
Aeko Social Backend Integration

AEKO now has a first-pass backend path for deterministic post hashing, Ed25519 signature verification, anchor transaction preparation, and persisted verification lookups for Aeko Social services.

npm install @aeko-chain/sdk
  • Reusable backend helpers in the Node SDK for canonical post payloads and signature verification.
  • A reference backend service with /social/posts/hash, /social/posts/verify, /social/posts/anchor, and verification lookup support.
  • Store adapter support so the reference flow can move from JSON persistence to Postgres or another production store.

Current Trust Model

The backend verifies signatures and AEKO Chain anchors immutable post hashes and metadata pointers. Full on-chain content-signature verification remains a follow-up step, not a requirement for the current production backend flow.

AEKO-20 Standard.title: AEKO-20 Standard
AEKO-20 Standard.html:
AEKO-20 Standard

AEKO-20 is the canonical fungible token standard for AEKO Chain. It is designed for transparent minting, transfer, burn, allowance, and future identity-aware transfer controls.

Core Capabilities

  • Authority-gated minting aligned to the tokenomics supply model
  • Transfers with sender validation and balance checks
  • Burning that reduces token supply
  • Allowance support via approve and transferFrom
  • Optional transfer hooks for identity or permissioned asset behavior

Planned Metadata Fields

  • Name
  • Symbol
  • Decimals
  • Supply cap
  • Optional metadata URI

Why It Matters

AEKO-20 is the base primitive for treasury assets, community tokens, app assets, and validator-emission-linked token flows across the AEKO ecosystem.

AEKO-721 Standard.title: AEKO-721 Standard
AEKO-721 Standard.html:
AEKO-721 Standard

AEKO-721 is the canonical NFT standard for AEKO Chain, intended for creator assets, collectibles, social objects, and royalty-aware media with creator-visible controls.

Core Capabilities

  • Collection initialization with authority ownership
  • NFT minting with unique token IDs and royalty basis points
  • Owner-signed transfer flow
  • Creator-controlled freeze and thaw actions
  • Creator or owner metadata updates with validation

Metadata Validation

  • Name and URI must be non-empty
  • URI fields must use accepted schemes like https://, ipfs://, or ar://
  • Description, image URI, and attributes are bounded for predictable indexer behavior

Creator Controls

Freeze / Thaw

Creators can freeze an NFT during moderation, dispute review, or compliance handling, then thaw it once cleared.

Metadata Evolution

Creators or current owners can refresh metadata while keeping creator, collection, and royalty linkage intact.

Demo Path

The current AEKO-721 demo lifecycle is: initialize collection, mint NFT, freeze, thaw, transfer, and update metadata.

Test Console Walkthrough.title: Test Console Walkthrough
Test Console Walkthrough.html:
Test Console Walkthrough

The Explorer test console lives at /network-tools. It uses the selected chain RPC for reads/transactions and the policy-controlled Funding Gateway for public-testnet wallet funding.

Test wallets only. Browser-generated keys are kept in localStorage. Do not use valuable production keys in the test console.

1. Generate a wallet

Create a test keypair and select it in the console.

2. Request testnet funding

On the public testnet, the console calls https://fund.aeko.online/api/funding/request. The Funding Gateway applies wallet cooldown and daily-budget policy, then makes a server-authorized low-level requestAirdrop RPC call.

3. Transfer between wallets

Transfers are built and signed in the browser, then submitted through sendTransaction.

Failure boundaries

  • Funding rate/cooldown: handled by the Funding Gateway.
  • Validator/RPC unavailable: chain reads and transaction submission fail until RPC recovers.
  • Faucet Daemon unavailable: funding requests fail server-side; users never connect to TCP 9900 directly.

Mini Feed (On-Chain SocialFi).title: Mini Feed (On-Chain SocialFi)
Mini Feed (On-Chain SocialFi).html:
Mini Feed (On-Chain SocialFi)

The Mini Feed tab in the test console is a real client of the social-posts native builtin. Every post and like is a Borsh-encoded instruction signed by the selected test wallet and submitted to the validator.

How posting works

  1. The browser calls getProgramAccounts on the social-posts program ([17;32]) to find the state account — created once by aeko-social-bootstrap.
  2. Your post body becomes the content_uri; SHA-256 hashes fill content_hash and metadata_hash.
  3. An AnchorPost instruction is built, signed with your test wallet, and sent via sendTransaction.
  4. The state account is polled every 8s; Borsh-decoded PostAnchor entries render as the timeline.

Likes

The heart button submits a RecordEngagement instruction with action_kind = Like. The wallet selected in the compose box pays the fee. Each (actor, post) pair can only like once — the on-chain replay guard rejects duplicates.

Operator prerequisites

If the feed shows "No social-posts state account on chain", the operator needs to run the bootstrap binary once:

AEKO_RPC_URL=http://validator:8899 \
  AEKO_PAYER_KEYPAIR=/keys/identity.json \
  aeko-social-bootstrap

In the testnet docker compose this is the one-shot social-bootstrap service. It is idempotent — re-runs no-op against an existing state account.

What is NOT here yet

  • Tipping (lives on social-monetization, not yet wired in the modal).
  • Replies / quotes — the on-chain types support them, the modal only emits Original for now.
  • Reward claims — social-rewards writes will land in a follow-up.

Explorer Troubleshooting.title: Explorer Troubleshooting
Explorer Troubleshooting.html:
Explorer Troubleshooting

If /explorer shows no blocks or transactions after activity on the chain, the explorer-backend indexer is what to debug — not the validator itself. Use the symptom guide below.

Symptom: Unexpected token 'B', "Bad Gateway" is not valid JSON

This message means the reverse proxy (Traefik / Coolify) returned an HTML 502 page and the browser tried to JSON-parse it. The frontend now intercepts that and shows a friendlier "Indexer is unreachable" message instead. Either way, the root cause is on the backend.

Most common cause: the indexer is configured to reach the validator over the public HTTPS hostname instead of the internal docker bridge. Fix in docker/compose.coolify.yml:

environment:
  AEKO_EXPLORER_RPC: http://validator:8899   # <-- internal hostname
  # NOT https://rpc.aeko.online

The HTTP server binds before catch-up runs, so the explorer port stays open even when the indexer can't reach the validator — the service looks "up" but returns empty arrays.

Symptom: empty /blocks and /transactions

The indexer is running but hasn't persisted anything yet. Three checks:

  1. docker logs aeko-explorer-backend — look for latest_slot() failed at boot or live sync tick failed.
  2. curl https://api.aeko.online/health — should return JSON, not HTML.
  3. Confirm the validator itself is making progress: curl -X POST https://rpc.aeko.online -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"getSlot"}'

Symptom: explorer worked, then went blank after a redeploy

The default explorer store is in-memory, so a restart wipes everything. To persist across deploys, set DATABASE_URL on the explorer-backend service to a Postgres DSN; the backend runs migrations on boot and switches to the durable store automatically.

SocialFi Bootstrap in Production.html:
SocialFi Bootstrap in Production

The five SocialFi programs are native builtins, but they each need one state account on chain before any read or write works. A dedicated social-bootstrap service creates these accounts automatically on the first deploy and no-ops on every deploy after. This page covers how it works, how to verify it ran, and what to do if it didn't.

How it runs

In docker/compose.coolify.yml the social-bootstrap service waits for validator to report service_healthy, then runs the aeko-social-bootstrap binary once. The binary:

  1. Polls getSlot until the validator advances past its first few slots (not just getHealth).
  2. Reuses persisted state keypairs from the social-state docker volume so re-deploys are idempotent.
  3. Submits create_account + program-specific InitializeState instructions, retrying transient failures with exponential backoff.
  4. Refuses to re-init an already-initialized account, so accidental double-runs are harmless.

Confirming it ran

docker logs aeko-social-bootstrap | tail -30

You're looking for five [social-…] init confirmed: <signature> lines, followed by the # Paste these into your dApp backend's env file summary. Or in the test console, open Programs — all five cards should read bootstrapped.

If a card shows "Initializing…" for longer than a minute

  1. Check the service is enabled in your Coolify stack. After pulling the latest compose file you need to redeploy so the new service appears.
  2. Inspect the logs. docker logs aeko-social-bootstrap tells you whether it's in the readiness wait, retrying sends, or already done.
  3. Check the payer has funds. The default payer is the genesis faucet (/keys/faucet.json); a missing or unfunded keypair will cause every send_and_confirm attempt to fail.
  4. Reset the chain only if the validator binary's builtin set is out of sync with the on-disk genesis. Set AEKO_RESET_LEDGER=1 in Coolify, redeploy, then unset it.

Re-running by hand

If you ever want to force a re-bootstrap on the live container without redeploying:

docker compose -f docker/compose.coolify.yml run --rm social-bootstrap

Because the keypair files persist in the social-state volume, this picks up the existing accounts; the chain rejects re-init and the run exits cleanly.

Frontend behavior

The Mini Feed and Programs tabs poll automatically every few seconds, so as soon as the bootstrap service finishes you'll see the "Initializing…" placeholder switch to a live feed and live KPI metrics without a page reload.
